b1-vilaghaboru-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Outbreak of War
b1-vilaghaboru-01.scenario: You are preparing for the citizenship interview. The examiner asks about the start of the First World War in 1914 and the Hungarian prime minister.
b1-vilaghaboru-01.prompt: Tell the examiner what Tisza István thought about the war and say what would have been different if he had stopped it.
cues: Say that Tisza opposed the war at first
Say that fewer soldiers would have fallen if he had stopped it
b1-vilaghaboru-01.target: Tisza István kezdetben ellenezte a háborút. Ha meg tudta volna akadályozni, nem esett volna el annyi magyar katona.
b1-vilaghaboru-01.english: István Tisza opposed the war at first. If he had been able to prevent it, so many Hungarian soldiers would not have fallen.
b1-vilaghaboru-01.canDo: I can say how the war began in 1914 and what István Tisza thought of it.

b1-vilaghaboru-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Home Front
b1-vilaghaboru-02.scenario: You are a guide at a museum exhibition about Budapest in the war. A visitor asks how people lived in 1916.
b1-vilaghaboru-02.prompt: Tell the visitor what the government had to introduce and who took the place of the men.
cues: Say what the government introduced
Say who took the men's places
b1-vilaghaboru-02.target: A kormány kénytelen volt bevezetni a jegyrendszert, és a női munkaerő vette át a bevonult férfiak helyét.
b1-vilaghaboru-02.english: The government was forced to introduce rationing, and women workers took the places of the men who had gone to war.
b1-vilaghaboru-02.canDo: I can describe daily life on the home front: rationing, shortages and women at work.

b1-vilaghaboru-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Isonzo Front
b1-vilaghaboru-03.scenario: You visit a village war memorial with a Hungarian friend. Your friend asks what Doberdó was.
b1-vilaghaboru-03.prompt: Tell your friend how many battles were fought at the Isonzo and where the soldiers fought.
cues: Say how many battles there were
Say where the soldiers fought
b1-vilaghaboru-03.target: Az Isonzónál tizenkét csatát vívtak, és a katonák a Doberdó-fennsíkon harcoltak.
b1-vilaghaboru-03.english: They fought twelve battles at the Isonzo, and the soldiers fought on the Doberdó plateau.
b1-vilaghaboru-03.canDo: I can describe the fighting at Doberdó on the Isonzo front in 1915–1917.

b1-vilaghaboru-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Aster Revolution
b1-vilaghaboru-04.scenario: At your citizenship interview, the examiner asks what happened in Budapest at the end of October 1918.
b1-vilaghaboru-04.prompt: Tell the examiner what the soldiers pinned on their caps and who formed a government.
cues: Say what the soldiers pinned on their caps
Say who formed the government
b1-vilaghaboru-04.target: A katonák őszirózsát tűztek a sapkájukra, és Károlyi Mihály alakított kormányt.
b1-vilaghaboru-04.english: The soldiers pinned asters on their caps, and Mihály Károlyi formed a government.
b1-vilaghaboru-04.canDo: I can describe the Aster Revolution of 1918 and name Mihály Károlyi.

b1-vilaghaboru-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of the Monarchy
b1-vilaghaboru-05.scenario: An evening-class teacher asks what happened in the Carpathian Basin at the end of 1918.
b1-vilaghaboru-05.prompt: Tell the teacher which troops advanced into Transylvania and what happened to most of the country.
cues: Say which troops advanced into Transylvania
Say that the old borders ended within weeks
b1-vilaghaboru-05.target: Román csapatok nyomultak Erdélybe, és az ország nagy része idegen csapatok kezére került.
b1-vilaghaboru-05.english: Romanian troops advanced into Transylvania, and most of the country came under foreign troops.
b1-vilaghaboru-05.canDo: I can describe how the Monarchy broke up at the end of 1918.

b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The First World War in Short
b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.scenario: At your citizenship interview the examiner asks you to sum up the First World War for Hungary.
b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.prompt: Tell the examiner when the war began and what happened to the Monarchy at the end.
cues: Say when the war began
Say what happened to the Monarchy
b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.target: A háború 1914-ben kezdődött, és a Monarchia 1918-ban felbomlott.
b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.english: The war began in 1914, and the Monarchy broke up in 1918.
b1-vilaghaboru-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up the First World War and the collapse of the Monarchy in a few sentences.

b1-trianon-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Peace Delegation
b1-trianon-01.scenario: At your citizenship interview, the examiner asks about the Hungarian delegation in Paris in 1920.
b1-trianon-01.prompt: Tell the examiner who led the delegation and why it showed Teleki Pál's Red Map.
cues: Say who led the delegation
Say why the Red Map was shown
b1-trianon-01.target: Apponyi Albert vezette a békedelegációt. A vörös térképet azért mutatták be, hogy megmutassák, hol élnek magyarok.
b1-trianon-01.english: Albert Apponyi led the peace delegation. The Red Map was shown to show where Hungarians live.
b1-trianon-01.canDo: I can describe how the Hungarian delegation argued for Hungary in Paris in 1920.

b1-trianon-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Signing
b1-trianon-02.scenario: You are a volunteer guide at a museum exhibition about Trianon. A visitor asks when the treaty was signed and what it changed.
b1-trianon-02.prompt: Tell the visitor the date of the signing and how much territory Hungary lost.
cues: Say the date of the signing
Say how much territory Hungary lost
b1-trianon-02.target: A trianoni békeszerződést 1920. június 4-én írták alá. Magyarország elveszítette területének több mint kétharmadát.
b1-trianon-02.english: The Trianon peace treaty was signed on 4 June 1920. Hungary lost more than two thirds of its territory.
b1-trianon-02.canDo: I can say when and where the Treaty of Trianon was signed and what it changed.

b1-trianon-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Life Beyond the Border
b1-trianon-03.scenario: A teacher at an evening class asks how the Hungarians beyond the new borders kept their culture.
b1-trianon-03.prompt: Tell the teacher what the Hungarian communities kept up.
cues: Say they kept up schools
Say they kept up newspapers and theatres
b1-trianon-03.target: A határon túli magyarok magyar iskolákat, lapokat és színházakat tartottak fenn.
b1-trianon-03.english: The Hungarians beyond the border kept up Hungarian schools, newspapers and theatres.
b1-trianon-03.canDo: I can describe the situation of Hungarians who found themselves outside Hungary's new borders.

b1-trianon-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Wagon Dwellers
b1-trianon-04.scenario: You visit a railway museum with a friend. A display is about the refugees of the early 1920s.
b1-trianon-04.prompt: Tell your friend where many refugee families lived in Budapest and why.
cues: Say where many families lived
Say why they lived there
b1-trianon-04.target: Sok menekült család vagonokban lakott, mert a fővárosban nem volt szabad lakás.
b1-trianon-04.english: Many refugee families lived in wagons because there was no free flat in the capital.
b1-trianon-04.canDo: I can describe the refugees and the 'wagon dwellers' of the early 1920s.

b1-trianon-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Day of National Unity
b1-trianon-05.scenario: At your citizenship interview, the examiner asks about 4 June.
b1-trianon-05.prompt: Tell the examiner what 4 June is called and since when.
cues: Say what 4 June is called
Say since when
b1-trianon-05.target: Június 4-e a Nemzeti Összetartozás Napja 2010 óta.
b1-trianon-05.english: 4 June has been the Day of National Unity since 2010.
b1-trianon-05.canDo: I can say what the Day of National Unity is and when it is held.

b1-trianon-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Trianon in Short
b1-trianon-consolidation.scenario: At your citizenship interview, the examiner asks you to sum up the Treaty of Trianon.
b1-trianon-consolidation.prompt: Tell the examiner when the treaty was signed and what it meant for Hungarians.
cues: Say when it was signed
Say what it meant for many Hungarians
b1-trianon-consolidation.target: A trianoni békeszerződést 1920. június 4-én írták alá, és több mint hárommillió magyar került határon túlra.
b1-trianon-consolidation.english: The Trianon peace treaty was signed on 4 June 1920, and more than three million Hungarians ended up beyond the border.
b1-trianon-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up the Treaty of Trianon and its effect on Hungarians in a few sentences.

b1-horthykorszak-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Regent
b1-horthykorszak-01.scenario: You are preparing for your citizenship interview. The examiner asks who led Hungary in the 1920s and what task the country faced.
b1-horthykorszak-01.prompt: Tell the examiner what parliament made Horthy in 1920 and that there were many tasks to be solved quickly.
cues: Say that parliament made Horthy the regent in 1920
Say that many tasks had to be solved urgently
b1-horthykorszak-01.target: 1920-ban a parlament kormányzóvá választotta Horthy Miklóst. Sok sürgősen megoldandó feladat várt rá.
b1-horthykorszak-01.english: In 1920 parliament elected Miklós Horthy regent. Many tasks that had to be solved urgently awaited him.
b1-horthykorszak-01.canDo: I can say who led Hungary after 1920 and what a kingdom without a king was.

b1-horthykorszak-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Stabilising the Money
b1-horthykorszak-02.scenario: In a museum about the 1920s your teacher asks how Hungary's money was put in order.
b1-horthykorszak-02.prompt: Tell your teacher that the League of Nations loan helped and that the pengő appeared in 1927.
cues: Say that the situation improved thanks to the League of Nations loan
Say when the pengő appeared
b1-horthykorszak-02.target: A Népszövetség kölcsöne révén javult a helyzet. Az új pénz, a pengő 1927-ben jött létre.
b1-horthykorszak-02.english: Thanks to the League of Nations loan the situation improved. The new money, the pengő, came into being in 1927.
b1-horthykorszak-02.canDo: I can say how Bethlen's government stabilised the economy and brought in the pengő.

b1-horthykorszak-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Schools for the Farms
b1-horthykorszak-03.scenario: On a visit to Szeged a museum guide asks why Klebelsberg had so many classrooms built.
b1-horthykorszak-03.prompt: Tell the guide that Klebelsberg had classrooms built so that every farmstead child could go to school.
cues: Say who had classrooms built and how many
Say what the aim was
b1-horthykorszak-03.target: Klebelsberg mintegy ötezer tantermet építtetett azzal a céllal, hogy minden tanyasi gyermek iskolába járhasson.
b1-horthykorszak-03.english: Klebelsberg had about five thousand classrooms built so that every child on the farmsteads could go to school.
b1-horthykorszak-03.canDo: I can describe Klebelsberg's school building and Szent-Györgyi's Nobel Prize.

b1-horthykorszak-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Titles and Addresses
b1-horthykorszak-04.scenario: In a coffeehouse exhibition your teacher asks how people addressed officials between the wars.
b1-horthykorszak-04.prompt: Tell your teacher how a minister and a state secretary were addressed.
cues: Say how a general was addressed
Say how a minister was addressed
b1-horthykorszak-04.target: Az államtitkárt Méltóságos úrnak, a minisztert Kegyelmes úrnak szólították.
b1-horthykorszak-04.english: A state secretary was addressed as Méltóságos úr, a minister as Kegyelmes úr.
b1-horthykorszak-04.canDo: I can describe the society of interwar Hungary, from the coffeehouses to the villages.

b1-horthykorszak-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The First Vienna Award
b1-horthykorszak-05.scenario: You are preparing for your citizenship interview. The examiner asks about 1938.
b1-horthykorszak-05.prompt: Tell the examiner that the First Vienna Award was announced after the Munich agreement.
cues: Say what was signed first
Say what was announced afterwards
b1-horthykorszak-05.target: Miután aláírták a müncheni egyezményt, kihirdették az első bécsi döntést.
b1-horthykorszak-05.english: After the Munich agreement was signed, the First Vienna Award was announced.
b1-horthykorszak-05.canDo: I can say what Hungary's foreign policy aimed at and what the First Vienna Award gave back.

b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Interwar Years in Review
b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the unit your teacher asks for a short summary of the interwar years for the citizenship interview.
b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.prompt: Tell the teacher who became prime minister in 1921 and who won a Nobel Prize in 1937.
cues: Say who became prime minister in 1921
Say who won the Nobel Prize in 1937
b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.target: 1921-ben Bethlen István lett a miniszterelnök. 1937-ben Szent-Györgyi Albert orvosi Nobel-díjat kapott.
b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.english: In 1921 István Bethlen became prime minister. In 1937 Albert Szent-Györgyi received the Nobel Prize in Medicine.
b1-horthykorszak-consolidation.canDo: I can review the main people and events of Hungary between the wars.

b1-masodikvh-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Kassa and the State of War
b1-masodikvh-01.scenario: You are preparing for your citizenship interview. The examiner asks what happened after the bombing of Kassa in June 1941.
b1-masodikvh-01.prompt: Tell the examiner who announced the state of war and what the army did as a consequence.
cues: Say who announced the state of war
Say what the army did as a consequence
b1-masodikvh-01.target: Bárdossy László bejelentette a hadiállapotot. A hadiállapot következtében a magyar hadsereg a keleti front felé indult.
b1-masodikvh-01.english: László Bárdossy announced the state of war. As a consequence of the state of war, the Hungarian army set off towards the Eastern Front.
b1-masodikvh-01.canDo: I can say how Hungary entered the war after the bombing of Kassa in 1941.

b1-masodikvh-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Don in January 1943
b1-masodikvh-02.scenario: A museum guide asks you about the Second Hungarian Army at the River Don.
b1-masodikvh-02.prompt: Tell the guide when the catastrophe happened and what the cold caused.
cues: Say when and where the catastrophe happened
Say what the extreme cold caused
b1-masodikvh-02.target: 1943 januárjában a Don mellett történt a katasztrófa. A rendkívüli hideg következtében sok katona megfagyott.
b1-masodikvh-02.english: The catastrophe happened by the Don in January 1943. As a consequence of the extreme cold, many soldiers froze to death.
b1-masodikvh-02.canDo: I can describe the Don catastrophe of January 1943 and the fate of the labour servicemen.

b1-masodikvh-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Remembering the Rescuers
b1-masodikvh-03.scenario: At a memorial in Budapest your teacher asks about 1944 and about the people who helped the persecuted.
b1-masodikvh-03.prompt: Tell your teacher when the Germans occupied Hungary and what Raoul Wallenberg did.
cues: Say the date of the German occupation
Say what Wallenberg did for the persecuted
b1-masodikvh-03.target: A németek 1944. március 19-én megszállták Magyarországot. Raoul Wallenberg kockáztatta az életét, és üldözötteket mentett meg.
b1-masodikvh-03.english: The Germans occupied Hungary on 19 March 1944. Raoul Wallenberg risked his life and saved persecuted people.
b1-masodikvh-03.canDo: I can describe the German occupation of 1944, the deportations and the rescuers.

b1-masodikvh-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Horthy's Armistice Attempt
b1-masodikvh-04.scenario: You are preparing for your citizenship interview. The examiner asks about October 1944.
b1-masodikvh-04.prompt: Tell the examiner how and when Horthy announced the armistice, and what happened to his attempt.
cues: Say when and where Horthy announced the armistice
Say what happened to the attempt
b1-masodikvh-04.target: Horthy 1944. október 15-én a rádióban jelentette be a fegyverszünetet. A kísérlet meghiúsult.
b1-masodikvh-04.english: Horthy announced the armistice on the radio on 15 October 1944. The attempt was thwarted.
b1-masodikvh-04.canDo: I can describe Horthy's failed armistice attempt and the Arrow Cross terror in 1944.

b1-masodikvh-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Bridges of Budapest
b1-masodikvh-05.scenario: On a walk along the Danube your teacher asks what happened to Budapest at the end of the war.
b1-masodikvh-05.prompt: Tell your teacher what the retreating Germans did to the bridges and what the capital became.
cues: Say what the Germans did to the bridges
Say what the capital turned into
b1-masodikvh-05.target: A visszavonuló németek felrobbantották a hidakat. A főváros romhalmazzá vált.
b1-masodikvh-05.english: The retreating Germans blew up the bridges. The capital turned into a pile of rubble.
b1-masodikvh-05.canDo: I can describe the siege of Budapest and the end of the war in 1945.

b1-masodikvh-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: World War II in Review
b1-masodikvh-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the unit your teacher asks for a short summary of 1944-1945 for the citizenship interview.
b1-masodikvh-consolidation.prompt: Tell the teacher who led the Arrow Cross Party and when the siege of Budapest ended.
cues: Say who led the Arrow Cross Party
Say when the siege ended
b1-masodikvh-consolidation.target: A nyilasokat Szálasi Ferenc vezette. Budapest ostroma 1945 februárjában ért véget.
b1-masodikvh-consolidation.english: The Arrow Cross was led by Ferenc Szálasi. The siege of Budapest ended in February 1945.
b1-masodikvh-consolidation.canDo: I can review the main events of Hungary in the Second World War.
